stage_2_story.text_en:
Avi wanted to build a bookcase for the hallway. He had been collecting books for years, and they were stacked in piles on the floor. One Sunday morning, he went to the hardware store and bought six wooden planks, a box of screws, and a small bottle of wood glue.

Back home, he cleared a space in the garage and laid out all his tools: the drill, the saw, the hammer, the level, the measuring tape, and a sheet of sandpaper. He started by measuring each plank carefully with the measuring tape and marking where to cut.

He put on his safety glasses and used the saw to cut the planks to the right lengths. The cutting made a lot of sawdust, so he swept the floor before moving on. Then he rubbed each cut edge with sandpaper until the wood felt smooth under his fingers.

Avi applied wood glue along the joints and held the pieces together. Then he pre-drilled small holes with the drill so the wood would not split. He drove each screw firmly into place. When the frame was assembled, he put the level on the top shelf to check that everything was straight. He had to loosen two screws and adjust slightly before it was perfectly level.

He carried the bookcase inside and placed it against the hallway wall. He used the hammer to tap in a few nails at the back to fix it to the wall so it would not fall forward. Miriam walked by and immediately started arranging books on the shelves. "You built this yourself?" she said, clearly impressed. Avi smiled. "Measure twice, cut once," he said.
